Issued at 126 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

Pattern Synopsis and Forecast:

Potent upper trough will continue to swing down into N MI this 
afternoon and evening, with burst of snow accompanying the lake 
instability and lift associated with this feature. Convective
boundary layer heights rise to around H700, plenty for vigorous
lake convection. Although temperatures start out marginal 
everywhere this afternoon, and even above freezing, temperatures
will fall with the southeastward push from the upper trough and
burst of snow, cooling more into the overnight as cold 
advection takes place. This burst of snow will result in rapid 
drops in visibility, quick accumulations on the roadways, and 
slick evening commuting conditions. A quick 1 to 2 inches of 
snow will be possible with this initial burst, especially across
traditional NW snowbelts from GT and Kalkaska counties up to
towards Otsego county. As cold advection filters into the 
overnight, lake effect is expected to continue with additional 
minor accumulations. The environment will be modest to start the
night, but lowering CBL heights, waning low level moisture, and
rising heights aloft will likely put an end to the accumulating
lake effect anyway. With an additional inch or maybe two 
overnight, current forecast has around 1 to 3 inches for NW 
snowbelts, potential exists for locally a little more for a few 
spots in Kalkaska and Otsego county. Consequently, the plan is 
to keep the region advisory free for the time being, perhaps a 
Special Weather Statement to capture the initial shock and awe 
of the burst of snow this afternoon and evening, but time will
tell. A small number of the post 12Z short range guidance is 
quite concerning with QPF potential and thus snow amounts for a
small area, but that seems to be the worst case scenario at this
time with the more reasonable within our forecast database. Will
update things accordingly if need be. Upper trough will be way 
to the east by early to midday Tuesday with higher heights 
filling in, thus, largely precipitation free through the day 
with light winds, but remaining relatively cold (although truly 
seasonable) with high temps in the 30s and low 40s. 

Airmass associated with our cold front from yesterday, and the 
reinforcing potent upper trough, will settle in over the region 
through midweek. Thus, temperatures will be much more seasonable, 
with 30s and low 40s for high temperatures through Wednesday. Dry 
conditions to remain in the forecast along with light winds.

Next period to watch will be Thursday into Friday. Upper low dives 
down from the N Plains into the Mid MS Valley Wednesday, interacting 
with a southern piece of energy along the Gulf Coast. These features 
interact, either in full or a fragmented piece of the southern 
stream phases with the northern upper low. The resultant 
northern upper low deepens and lifts northward into the Ohio
Valley/Appalachia Thursday into Friday. At the sfc, the mess of
energy from these two upper lows will product an area of low 
pressure likely inland of the coast (inland cutter) to some 
degree. Note there is plenty of spread in the ensembles, ranging
from the low pressure system from Ohio to just off the NJ 
coast, which has to do with how the two aforementioned pieces of
energy interact with each other and where the dominant sfc low 
resides. If the main upper low/sfc low is farther east, much 
less in the way of precip is expected (00Z ECMWF) but farther 
west and more precipitation, of the rain/snow mix variety (mix
for the higher terrain as the sfc temperatures will be quite
marginal). Be that as it may, the upper support displaced from 
the northern upper low could still produce showers across the 
area, most notably Thursday night into Friday. Tough to pin down
specific details, but best guess at this time is for rain 
showers to move in later Thursday into Friday, with some 
rain/snow for the higher terrain. Not seeing any support for any
significant snow accums at this time, nor rain with a low 
chance (10-40%) for 0.5" or more of rain in the ensemble 
guidance (there is a gradient in probs across central MI, due to
the spread in the guidance). Overall though, northeast lower 
will be favored for precip due to the track of the upper level 
and sfc features. Something to watch going forward. Another 
system likely skirts down out of the north for this weekend, 
with the potential for additional rain/snow mix chances. Temps
look to remain 40s for this weekend.
